title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Papua New Guinea: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Papua New Guinea: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Papua New Guinea: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: Preparing medical, workplace, superannuation, civil registration, and legal records in advance in Papua New Guinea enables patients and families to act clearly within national legal rules and provincial hospital capacity. Organizing beneficiary nominations, Will storage, and tax numbers early prevents complex delays across superannuation funds, banks, and the National Court [1][3][7][11].

steps.title: Clinical and palliative coordination plus Employment Act sick leave
steps.html:
• Coordinate specialist inpatient, outpatient, and palliative care services through the National Department of Health framework (health.gov.pg) and referral centres such as Port Moresby General Hospital (111 24/7 emergency; #115 toll-free; +675 324 8100 switchboard; +675 324 8200 / 8300 emergency direct) [12][13]. Discuss treatment preferences directly with the treating physician while capacity is clear [12].
  • Under the Employment Act 1978 (Chapter 373), eligible employees with at least 6 months of continuous service earn 6 days of paid sick leave per year under Section 65, cumulative up to 18 days exclusive of the current year [14]. To qualify for paid sick leave, employees must notify the employer within 72 hours and present a registered medical practitioner's certificate (s. 65(4)), alongside 14 consecutive days of annual recreation leave (s. 61) [14].
  • Employees working away from their home province on attested contracts should also note employer duties under Sections 42 and 42A for return transport of dependants and remains if repatriation becomes necessary [14].

steps.title: Drafting a Will, estate planning, and Office of the Public Trustee
steps.html:
• Execute or update a formal written Will satisfying signature and witness requirements under the Wills Act and the Wills, Probate and Administration Act 1966 (paclii.org) so executors have clear authority for National Court filings [1][2].
  • Review how customary land vs. alienated title and bank accounts are held: customary land transfers follow local land-tenure rules rather than standard testamentary transfer, while cash, vehicles, superannuation, and registered property depend on proper Wills and nominations [1][10].
  • Where institutional administration or Will safekeeping is appropriate, review estate management, trust, and minor-beneficiary services available from Office of the Public Trustee (+675-301-2800, publictrustee@justice.gov.pg) under the Public Curator Act (Cap. 81) [3]. Clarify financial Powers of Attorney with a PNG lawyer if trusted relatives need authority to manage banking during serious illness [1][3].

steps.title: Superannuation nominations and medical early-withdrawal checks
steps.html:
• Audit beneficiary nomination schedules and member contact details directly with the relevant PNG superannuation fund, because outdated or conflicting nominations frequently delay payouts [6][7][10].
  • For Nasfund members (+675 313 1800 / shortcode 1588 / help@nasfund.com.pg), review medical incapacity and health-interrupted withdrawal requirements through Nasfund's superannuation access rules and e-Branch portal [6][7][8].
  • For Nambawan Super Limited contributors (180 1599 toll-free call centre), inspect registered beneficiary designations and acceptable identity document rules on file [9][10].

steps.title: Civil identity alignment and Internal Revenue Commission (IRC) tax files
steps.html:
• Check spelling consistency across birth certificates, marriage certificates, national identification (NID) documents held with the PNG Civil and Identity Registry (PNGCIR), passports, and bank records so claims match without discrepancy [4][5].
  • Verify active Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) status, salary/wage tax records, and any business lodgements with Internal Revenue Commission (IRC) (irc.gov.pg), noting that Tax Clearance Certificates (TCC) may be required for certain cross-border remittances [11][16]. Papua New Guinea does not levy a separate inheritance or estate tax [11].
  • Keep original executed Wills, property titles, insurance policies, and TIN notices stored together in a known secure folder [1][3][11].

steps.title: Cross-border legalisation readiness and household inventory
steps.html:
• Confirm overseas authentication requirements early if assets, pensions, or family members reside outside PNG: because Papua New Guinea is not a Contracting Party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention, PNG vital records and court documents used abroad require diplomatic or consular legalisation rather than a Hague Apostille [15].
  • Assemble a clear written dossier listing superannuation member numbers (Nasfund or Nambawan Super), PNGCIR ID details, IRC TIN, bank accounts, employer HR contacts, and Will storage location [3][7][9][11].
  • Verify international remittance rules and commercial bank signatory requirements early where cross-border family support is planned [11][15].

prefillQuestion: A family member is facing a serious or terminal illness in Papua New Guinea. We need an overview of the main official steps and contacts in Papua New Guinea for palliative care, powers of attorney, advance directives, and caregiver support.

contacts.name: Port Moresby General Hospital
contacts.note: 24/7 Emergency line: 111; Emergency direct: +675 324 8200 / +675 324 8300; Toll-Free: #115. Provides inpatient and palliative care wards.

contacts.name: Office of the Public Trustee
contacts.note: Administers Wills storage, trust services, and deceased or minor estate protection within DJAG.

contacts.name: Nasfund
contacts.note: Call Centre +675 313 1800, shortcode 1588, WhatsApp 8368 9873; handles medical incapacity withdrawals and beneficiary nominations.

contacts.name: Nambawan Super Limited
contacts.note: Toll-Free Call Centre 180 1599 (Mon-Fri 8:00 AM-5:00 PM) for beneficiary updates and member withdrawal guidance.

contacts.name: Internal Revenue Commission (IRC)
contacts.note: Manages TIN registration, personal income tax filings, and Tax Clearance Certificates (TCC).
